ai.thread_title: Opus 5.5: New capabilities in vision, coding, 3D and UI generation

Vision and 3D modeling improved significantly; cost remains lower than prior generation

ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Multiple independent, credible technical signals from practitioners shipping real work with it.

ai.thread_title: DeepSeek publishes detailed inference architecture; Western Twitter sees only summaries

ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Signals a blind spot in Western AI builder circles; actionable if DeepSeek becomes a cost-competitive option for your clients.

ai.thread_title: New Claude Projects enables multi-agent coordination with message-passing threads
ai.name: Anthropic / Ethan Mollick (reporting)
ai.hook: Claude Projects redesigned for **multi-agent work**: user-facing coordinator model spawns independent agent threads with message passing.
insights: Solves group-chat chaos: structured workflow instead of flat conversation
Coordinator model + worker agents handle distinct tasks in parallel threads
Requires setup fiddling but enables powerful agent orchestration at scale
ai.for_you: Direct tool for your agency: use this for client workflows requiring multiple specialized agents (e.g., one agent drafts content, another reviews, third optimizes for PT SMBs). Test this week to build a reusable agent template.

ai.reason: Ethan Mollick flagged it as a practical interface for agent workflows; directly applicable to agency delivery.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Independent practitioner validating the tool; high engagement signal; clear use case for your workflows.

ai.thread_title: Agent swarms as compute scaling: moving beyond single-agent constraints
ai.name: Aaron Levie / Aditya Agarwal
ai.hook: Agent swarms enable **compute-intensive parallelization** of work previously bottlenecked by single-agent token limits.
insights: Inference-time scaling → subagents → agent swarms mirrors CPU → multi-core → distributed systems evolution
Massive token consumption shift: agent work (background tasks) is 100-1000x higher token volume than chatting
Work in the economy constrained by **available compute**, not by availability of algorithms
ai.for_you: Fundamental shift for your agency model: you can now offer background agent workflows (content repurposing, lead scoring, client data enrichment) that scale with compute budgets, not human time. This multiplies your delivery capacity and shifts margins from implementation to infrastructure.
ai.context: This is a business model insight, not a tool announcement. It signals that the next wave of AI agency work will be agent swarms running background tasks, consuming 10-100x more tokens than current chat-based work.
ai.what_changed: Multiple credible builders (Levie, Agarwal) independently flagging the same pattern: compute is now the critical variable in agent economics.
ai.reason: Changes how you price and scope agency work. If background swarms consume 100-1000x tokens, your cost basis and margins shift materially.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Multiple independent signals converging on the same insight; directly affects your agency pricing model.

ai.thread_title: Ethan Mollick's 'Co-Existence' out now; guides living/working when AI sometimes beats humans
ai.name: Ethan Mollick
ai.hook: New book released today: practical guide to **coexisting with AI** when capability is uneven and unpredictable.
insights: Book website built with Opus 5.5; interactive experience demonstrates the concept
Core thesis: AI is sometimes, but not always, better than humans; coexistence is the frame, not obsolescence or supremacy
Aimed at professionals navigating uncertainty of AI capabilities
ai.for_you: Useful frame for positioning your agency to Portuguese SMB clients: emphasize coexistence, not replacement. Your clients want AI that makes their teams better, not AI that makes their teams irrelevant. Mollick's book validates that positioning.
ai.what_changed: Book is live; Mollick used Opus 5.5 to build the website, demonstrating the tech in real product.
ai.reason: Frames the right mental model for client conversations; useful reference for positioning your agency's value.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: High-signal practitioner releasing a full book; frames the zeitgeist for AI agency work.

podcasts.episode: AI in NYC: How Tenex Builds an AI-Native Engineering Team — Alex Lieberman & CJ Hess
podcasts.takeaway: AI-native SDLC pays engineers for outcomes, not implementation; agents do the implementation, humans do planning and review.
key_points: MetaHarness process: version control for plans, decisions, and project context; agents consume this to reduce planning overhead

Token economics: long-running agent tasks consume 10-100x tokens of typical chat; ROI depends on margin per task, not margin per token
podcasts.for_you: Framework for your agency: structure client projects around outcome-based pricing with agents handling implementation. Track token spend per client task to understand your real margins. Use version control for client context and project decisions so agents can pick up mid-project work.

tech.hook: Use controlled languages (ASD-STE100), voice rambles, and large token budgets to extract reasoning from language models.
tech.key_point: Model outputs need **long rambles and structured prompts** to surface reasoning; lazy typing misses depth available in the model.
tech.for_you: When debugging agent behavior for your clients, use voice input and ask for explanations in controlled language. This surfaces model reasoning that text input would miss.
